About Us

We are a team of neuroscientists, mathematicians, AI researchers, and engineers on a mission to learn from the human brain and to build an AI that can learn continuously, in a sample-efficient way, and reason about its knowledge. We are a seed-stage team with early commercial traction building
**Cortex**

. Cortex is in use by customers today, and we're only just beginning in terms of research and capabilities.

About the role

We're looking for an
**AI research engineer**

to bring ideas and execution toward understanding natural intelligence and implementing it in silico. You'll develop the next iteration of Cortex and test it against hard challenges (like ARC-AGI and others). You'll also help design and publish new algorithms, approaches, and capabilities for Cortex, inspired by the brain and specifically focused on sample-efficient continuous learning and explicit knowledge representation. You'll create and publish new benchmarks that set the bar for the capabilities of Cortex and all next-generation thinking machines.

Your near-term research focus will be on post-training techniques, novel reward models, differentiable approaches to explicit memory stores, harness improvements, native multimodality, and direct application of existing neuroscience research to Cortex.

Longer-horizon research goals we expect you to participate in include exploring non-transformer architectures, novel information encoding approaches, and beyond. We expect to push the envelope from "interdisciplinary" work to "a new, named field of science" and you will be part of it.

What you'll do

As a Research Engineer, you'll bring both engineering discipline and research taste. You will work with our research scientists and mathematicians to explore and publish. You'll work with our engineers to translate this into product. Your primary outputs will be both publications and code artifacts, about a 50/50 split. We do not have an open source strategy yet; come help define it.

* Develop the next iteration of Cortex, and benchmark it against hard, long-horizon challenges in agentic reasoning, continual learning, and knowledge use.
* Participate in the design and publishing of new benchmarks and evaluations that expose failure modes in how AI systems learn, represent, and use knowledge.
* Research brain-inspired approaches to learning and knowledge representation: how knowledge is structured, linked, updated, resolved, and forgotten, drawing on neuroscience and cognitive science, as well as modern AI research.
* Improve the agentic harness around Cortex: planning, search, tool use, query understanding, and grounded abstention.
* Apply and evaluate post-training techniques (fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, distillation) where they improve sample-efficient, continual learning.
* Author papers and technical reports, and help shape our research direction.
* Land research in the product, working with the engineering team to take ideas from experiment to production with tests and regression gates.
